sections.kicker: Prepared for byad.studio by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: byad.studio has one sharp offer. The bio leads with the line every studio uses.
sections.keep: "Brand Essentials in 3 weeks". A specific offer with a specific time, which most studios never say.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet
first.

pins.quote: Brand & web design studio for founders
pins.what: The first line describes any studio on Instagram.
pins.why: Founders scroll past a dozen of these a day, which is the thing that feels off.
pins.how: Name who you design for and what changes for them.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: People see a studio, not a reason to pick yours.

pins.what: Your clearest promise sits on the second line.
pins.why: A fixed scope and a fixed time is a reason to choose you, and it is easy to sell.
pins.how: Make it the first thing people read, and build the grid around it.
pins.label: Your offer
pins.cost: The offer that sells itself waits behind a line that does not.

pins.what: The name says one designer; the bio says a studio.
pins.why: People do not know if they are hiring Adelaida or a team.
pins.how: Pick one. A named designer is a strength when you are starting.
pins.label: Your name
pins.cost: Prospects hesitate on who they would work with.

sections.intro: You said something feels off and you are just starting. Starting is the best time to fix this. Here is what stood out on your Instagram.

sections.body: It is 20 minutes with me. We go through this page together, on byad.studio's own screens, and you leave knowing what to change first.
sections.note: A few short questions first, then you pick a time. You can also just reply to the email.

reference: Muji, from another category. It never says it is a store for everyone. It says what it leaves out.
